name: Green River Gorge
gaugeName: Green River at Purification Plant near Palmer
blurb: A sheer-walled sandstone gorge an hour from Seattle — spring whitewater controlled by Howard Hanson Dam.

sections.notes: Class II–III whitewater. Headworks is controlled raft and kayak access through the Tacoma Water security gate; check in and follow the guard’s current instructions. No inner-tubing, swimming or general recreation inside the controlled access area. Take out at Kanaskat-Palmer’s upper hand-access site before the harder park rapids. Discover Pass required at the park.

notices.title: Check park gates and river-access signs
notices.text: State Parks lists these day-use areas open for winter 2026–27, with possible temporary weather closures. Hand-launch sites and the actual shore entry may differ from the Area marker. Check current park alerts before setting your shuttle.

notices.title: Controlled raft and kayak launch
notices.text: Tacoma Water identifies a designated boating launch below its diversion. Check in at the guard station before entering; bring identification and vehicle insurance documentation and follow current permit, parking and daylight rules. The watershed is not open for general recreation or inner-tubing.

notices.title: Use the upper Kanaskat take-out
notices.text: Scout the upper hand-access site during your shuttle. The park map warns of Class IV water beyond it; do not continue to the lower access expecting the same difficulty. The Area marker shows the upper day-use vicinity, not the precise exit.

sections.routeReview: Approximate Green River course overview from the designated Headworks access vicinity toward the upper Kanaskat take-out. The line shows general bends and does not identify a landing connection, safe rapid line, navigation route or remaining-time estimate.

sections.notes: Mercury and Nozzle are Class IV. Remote, steep-walled gorge with few exits — experienced boaters only. Discover Pass required at both Kanaskat-Palmer and Flaming Geyser state parks.

notices.text: The park map distinguishes upper and lower hand-launch sites. Class IV water occurs below the upper site; this gorge trip is for experienced whitewater boaters. The marker shows the upper day-use vicinity, not a precise entry or a rapid-avoidance route.
